context.careSetting: Fictional adult general-medicine follow-up outpatient clinics, England
context.population: Adult outpatient attendees, including encounters with more than one speaker
context.intendedUse: Draft outpatient consultation notes for treating clinician review before entry into the EPR; no diagnosis, triage, prescribing or autonomous actions.
context.proposedDecision: Fictional project team proposes proceeding with deployment across these clinics on the basis that mandated clinician sign-off and a local SOP sufficiently mitigate inaccurate notes, and assigns a provisional 'Low' residual-risk category.

contextDimensions.description: Some 15-minute consultations involve a relative or more than one speaker.
Notes are copied from a stand-alone browser after clinician editing and before EPR signing.

hazards.hazardousSituation: An AVT-generated note may omit, misattribute or invent clinically relevant encounter details.
hazards.potentialHarm: An undetected inaccurate signed record could influence subsequent management or safety-netting.

hazards.hazardousSituation: A note edited in the stand-alone AVT interface may differ from the content finally copied into and signed in the EPR.
hazards.potentialHarm: An incorrect or outdated final record could affect downstream care.

controls.statement: Treating clinician reviews and signs each generated note, including comparison of clinically significant details before copying to EPR.
controls.mechanismExplanation: Clinician compares clinically significant encounter details against the draft before EPR sign-off, as proposed in the case.
dependencyIds: Time and opportunity to check the note
Corrected note matching the EPR version

controls.statement: Manual copying of the edited note into the EPR followed by clinician sign-off.
dependencyIds: AVT and EPR draft versions remain aligned
Final text is the reviewed text

evidence.title: TheHill and Oxford University Hospitals: Ambient Voice Technology in Acute Services - An Evaluation
limitations: Service evaluation; no randomisation or control group
Self-reported, heterogeneous and not designed for systematic patient-outcome or error tracking
Editing frequency is not patient-harm frequency or local clinician-review sensitivity
Reported reason categories may overlap; source calls 24/398 6.2% although this ratio does not exactly equal 6.2%
